title: What TAP on Doge is
text: TAP is an inscribed token protocol from the Trac ecosystem. On Dogecoin it is carried by Doginals inscriptions and externally mirrors DRC-20.

title: What Dogecoin actually changes
text: Block target, inscription carrier, size and fees, large content across transactions, and address format. Five differences that change how you should act.

title: A confirmation is a unit of time
text: Six confirmations is about six minutes on Dogecoin and about an hour on Bitcoin. Elapsed time is not accumulated work.

title: The operations, at a glance
text: All eleven TAP operations with their group and whether they must be tapped. Every token operation name is prefixed.

title: Support in Bitcoin Universe products
text: Marketplace feature gated in external execution mode, wallet view send receive, Inscribe mint. Sell is unsupported.

title: Related protocols and where TAP sits
text: DRC-20, Doginals, Dogemap, DMT, and TAP on Bitcoin, and how each relates to TAP on Doge.

title: Reporting a security issue
text: Report vulnerabilities privately through GitHub private vulnerability reporting on this repository. Never open a public issue.

title: Scope and conformance
text: Dogecoin mainnet only. Rules originate with the Trac Systems Dogecoin TAP specification; Bitcoin Universe decisions are labelled.

title: The Doginals envelope
text: Push data in the signature script of input 0. The literal ord, a piece count, a content type, then countdown and chunk pairs of at most 520 bytes.

title: Partial inscriptions and reveal chains
text: When the pushes run out the parse continues into the next transaction. If the chain ends before the countdown reaches zero, nothing is indexed.

title: Payload encoding
text: One JSON object, p must be exactly tap, op must be one of eleven names, amounts are decimal strings, tickers are measured in Unicode symbols.

title: Ticker length rules by height
text: Exactly 3 or 5 to 32 Unicode symbols below block 5,487,639. From that height, 1 to 32.

title: Identifiers
text: Inscription ids are txid plus i plus index. Dogecoin addresses are base58check, version 0x1e for P2PKH and 0x16 for P2SH, case-sensitive.

title: Tapping
text: Sending an inscription from the address that holds it back to that same address. Every internal operation needs it; the external token operations do not.

title: token-deploy
text: Creates a ticker with a maximum supply and an optional per-mint limit. A second deployment of the same ticker is invalid.

title: token-mint
text: Mints from a deployed ticker within its per-mint limit. A privileged deployment requires a signed prv object naming the permitted address.

title: token-transfer
text: Parks an amount as a transfer inscription. There is no recipient field; the recipient is chosen later by sending the inscription.

title: token-send
text: Moves many amounts of many tickers to many recipients. Atomic on syntax before the tap, per item on semantics at the tap.

title: block-transferables and unblock-transferables
text: Disables or re-enables incoming inscribe transfers for the tapping address. Exists to stop grief attacks against authority addresses.

title: token-trade
text: Create, cancel, or fill an inscription-based trade. Filling with a fee receiver charges a fixed 0.3 percent in the purchased token.

title: token-auth
text: Create, use, or cancel a signing authority that issues redeems. Anyone may inscribe a signed redeem and no tap is required for it.

title: privilege-auth
text: Gates who may mint a deployment and records signed statements binding a file hash to an address. seq must be a JSON integer, never a string.

title: dmt-deploy and dmt-mint
text: Element fields 4, 10 and 11 are supported. From block 5,497,100 field numbers and blk must be precise rather than read with parseInt rules.

title: State model and balances
text: Available plus transferable equals total. Only available balance can be spent by a new operation. A transfer inscription is live, then consumed.

title: Activation heights
text: 4,600,000 first indexed inscription height. 4,771,259 ord wallet 1.0.1 and Dogemap. 5,487,639 ticker widening. 5,497,100 precise DMT values.

title: Invalid conditions
text: Every condition under which a message creates no TAP state, with the rule number that governs it.

title: Defects in the published text
text: Three Bitcoin artefacts survive in the published Dogecoin specification: the valid Bitcoin addresses wording, the bech32 example addresses, and a Bitcoin privilege activation height.

title: What you need
text: A Dogecoin wallet that speaks Doginals and can send a chosen inscription, DOGE for fees and postage, and a TAP indexer you trust.

title: Worked example: a mint
text: Commit, reveal, confirm, credit. A mint is not tapped and takes effect on its own confirmation.

title: Worked example: a transfer
text: Park then send. Step one moves nothing to anybody; it moves your own balance from available to transferable.

title: Worked example: a batch send
text: Inscribe to your own address, wait, then tap. Unfunded items are skipped individually at tapping time.

title: Choosing a confirmation count
text: A table of confirmation counts in elapsed time on both chains, and why time is not the same as accumulated work.

title: What supports TAP on Doge
text: Only capabilities verifiable in the Bitcoin Universe codebase. Third-party tools are not certified here.

title: A draft that uses the DRC-20 operation names
text: A payload with p tap and a bare mint or transfer confirms, costs a full fee, and is then indexed by nobody. There is no retry and no recovery.

title: A Bitcoin address in a Dogecoin payload
text: The published specification inherited Bitcoin example addresses. Recipients must be Dogecoin base58check addresses.

title: Tooling that builds a Bitcoin witness envelope
text: The Dogecoin parser reads push data only and stops at the first non-push opcode, so a witness envelope inscribes nothing.

title: An interrupted reveal chain
text: The inscription does not exist rather than being truncated. Every fee already paid is spent and the missing pieces cannot be supplied later.

title: Assuming Bitcoin byte economics
text: Dogecoin has no witness and no discount. Every byte including pretty-printing whitespace is charged at full rate.

title: Forgetting postage
text: The output carrying an inscription must stay above the dust threshold, which is far higher in nominal units on Dogecoin.

title: Terminology
text: Doginals, envelope, piece count, partial inscription, tapping, available, transferable, total, consumed, authority, quarantine, checkpoint, koinu, Dogemap.

title: Confirmation semantics
text: A row with a block height is confirmed; a row without is pending. Messages apply in confirmation order, and a tapped operation needs two confirmations.

title: Mempool semantics
text: The Bitcoin Universe Dogecoin TAP source has no mempool feed and does not claim complete pending activity. Absence of a pending row proves nothing.

title: Reorg behaviour
text: At most 5 savepoints every 10 blocks within 25 blocks of the tip, recovering roughly 40 to 49 blocks, which on a one-minute chain is under an hour.

title: Fees and size
text: No witness and no discount, fees quoted per kilobyte of the whole transaction, chunks of at most 520 bytes, and a stepped cost once a reveal chain begins.

title: The Bitcoin Universe Dogecoin TAP source
text: Partial coverage, indexed tip published alongside the chain tip and the lag, no floating-point decimal conversion, quarantine rather than guessing.

title: Limitations
text: No mempool truth, no protocol-level reversal, no recovery from a partial reveal, no arbitration between authorities, no on-chain balance.

title: Security considerations
text: Confirmation counts do not port between chains, read every pre-filled payload, verify addresses on this chain, protect inscription outputs from being spent as change.

text: The decisions an indexer must make explicitly, each with the rule that governs it, from which input to parse through to how to report a checkpoint.

title: Rejected payloads
text: Payloads that create no state, including the DRC-20 operation names, a Bitcoin recipient, a string seq, and an inscription number used where an id is required.

text: Paste a payload and see errors, cautions, and notes. Runs entirely in your browser; nothing is transmitted or stored.

title: What the validator cannot check
text: It sees one payload. It cannot know whether a ticker is deployed, whether supply remains, or whether a signature verifies.
